newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, Chubais discuss taxes at regular meeting.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, Chubais discuss taxes at regular meeting.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin and his chief of staff Anatoly Chubais discussed Russia's poor tax collection and rising wage arrears on Thursday, Yeltsin's press office said.
A statement released after the meeting, in the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow, said Yeltsin had ordered government officials to declare their income for 1996.

Yeltsin, 65, has been in Barvikha since the weekend and has met several officials there. Before then he spent over three weeks in a Moscow hospital while doctors prepared him for heart surgery, expected in the next two months.
The statement said Yeltsin described the current wage situation as unacceptable.

"Students, teachers, the military and other workers in the state sphere are not receiving wages because a number of big enterprises are literally taking the finances of the country by the throat and refusing to pay taxes," he said.
The statement said the meeting lasted for about an hour.

Tax evasion is one of the biggest economic problems facing the Russian government this year and revenue lags well below budgeted levels. Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin has said he expects collection rates to improve in October or November.
Wage arrears are also a major issue and workers across Russia have gone on strike to complain that they have not been paid for months.
